## TL;DR

Remote browser captures now publish their result atomically and exit after bounded cleanup. The Tailscale Docker collector can recover a completed capture without waiting for its container to exit. Failed handoffs cancel that task’s outstanding captures, and the host sweep can reap quiet, completed orphan containers.

## Work and rationale

The runner writes a temporary result and renames it into place, bounds preview shutdown, logs the outcome and explicitly exits. The collector polls the unique run’s artifact directory, checks that the result is stable and parseable inside the container, removes only that container, and downloads the existing artifacts through the normal channel. It records force collection in the task’s remote events. The idle-host sweep verifies the capture mode, completion log, two minutes of silence, and low CPU immediately before removing an orphan; the system log records why it was reaped.

Failed handoffs request cancellation through the remote validator. The Tailscale pool removes matching queued shot jobs, targets active shot containers by their unique names, aborts their SSH and upload work, and invalidates the cancelled generation to prevent retry or a late dispatch. Other tasks and validation jobs are not selected. The UI gate also cancels when waiting for another capture times out.

## Approaches tried

Focused tests exercised the actual Bun entry with a lingering timer, the collection and reaper shell commands using a fake Docker executable, pool cancellation, and handoff failure. The tests check that recent output or active CPU protects a capture and that an unrelated queued task remains in the pool. A runner-level test exercises collection while the original SSH run is still open, and another exercises cancellation of a running and queued capture. The final `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed, including remote tests, browser audit, smoke, build, format and lint.

## Challenges and blockers

Remote runner scripts are installed independently on hosts, so collection and reaping are implemented on the control plane and do not depend on deploying a changed host script. No live remote runner was exercised in this session. The collector currently targets Tailscale Docker captures; native runner and Hetzner paths retain their existing behavior.

## Key learnings

The result precedes preview shutdown, so cleanup needs its own deadline. Capture identity must remain run-specific when a failed handoff and a retry overlap; cancellation must also reach both the queue and an already leased container.
